definition: The olympiad-level competition-mathematics set that 14 archived efficient-reasoning papers use as the hard end of their maths suite, above MATH-500, AMC23 and GSM8K and alongside AIME. It is repeatedly where token savings run out: ReBalance cuts only 2.6-17.6% of tokens on OlympiadBench against 26.8-30.2% on AMC23 and 14.4-35.4% on GSM8K for the same models, and AutoThink's DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B scores 44.8% here against 84.0% on MATH. It is also where accuracy is given up first: ThreadWeaver's parallel-threaded Qwen3-8B reaches 63.5% against 65.0% for its sequential GRPO baseline, while Refining Over Resampling buys 47.2% against 41.0% for the strongest verifier baseline only by spending extra self-correction rounds. One archived multimodal paper (Real-Time Visual Attribution Streaming) uses it as a vision-language maths category rather than a text-only one, so what a paper means by 'OlympiadBench' is not identical across the archive.

evidence.note: Uses integrated-gradient token attribution, aggregated into per-segment strength and direction-consistency scores, to pick which segments of a long chain-of-thought an SFT run should compute loss on, masking the rest.
evidence.title: Segment-Level Attribution for Selective Learning of Long Reasoning Traces

evidence.note: QLPO is a GRPO variant that leaves the reward, advantage estimator and update untouched and instead over-generates K=16 rollouts per prompt and resamples the M=8 training group to favour short-correct and long-incorrect trajectories, which shortens outputs by 30-70% relative to GRPO at roughly unchanged accuracy.
evidence.title: QLPO: Quadrant-weighted Sampling for Length-aware Policy Optimization

evidence.note: A training-free, verifier-free test-time scaling method that refines each of N sampled reasoning rollouts through D rounds of self-critique and self-correction before majority-voting the answers, instead of only sampling more candidates or relying on an external verifier.
evidence.title: Refining Over Resampling: Test-Time Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning

evidence.note: ThinkBooster is a unified, open-source framework (Python library + OpenAI-compatible proxy endpoint + visual debugger) implementing 9 test-time-compute scaling strategies and 4 scorer families under a joint TFLOPs-and-tokens compute-accounting benchmark, whose pilot study finds PRM scorers dominate on math while lightweight uncertainty scorers are surprisingly competitive on (out-of-domain-for-PRM) coding tasks, and that beam search often underperforms best-of-N and even self-consistency despite costing more compute.
evidence.title: ThinkBooster: A Unified Framework for Seamless Test-Time Scaling of LLM Reasoning

evidence.note: DTSR (Dynamic Thought Sufficiency in Reasoning) is a training-free early-exit framework where the model itself, at each reflection signal ('Wait', 'Alternatively', etc.), evaluates from a third-person perspective whether its own chain-of-thought so far is sufficient to answer, exiting once a self-assessed sufficiency score crosses a threshold, cutting reasoning length 28.9-34.9% with near-zero accuracy loss across Qwen3-8B/14B/32B and five benchmarks, outperforming NoThinking, NOWAIT, and DEER while also cutting inference latency 25-40% (unlike DEER, which reduces length but increases latency).
evidence.title: When Is Thinking Enough? Early Exit via Sufficiency Assessment for Efficient Reasoning

evidence.note: AutoThink uses a three-stage RL curriculum with stage-wise reward shaping to teach R1-style distilled models to decide per problem whether to emit an explicit reasoning chain at all.
evidence.title: Learning When to Think: Shaping Adaptive Reasoning in R1-Style Models via Multi-Stage RL

evidence.note: ConPress observes that a reasoning model shortens its traces when several independent questions share one prompt, and harvests those shortened traces as self-supervised fine-tuning data for the single-question setting.
evidence.title: ConPress: Learning Efficient Reasoning from Multi-Question Contextual Pressure

evidence.note: DiffAdapt trains a small probe on a reasoning model's hidden state to classify each question as Easy/Normal/Hard and picks a matching prompt, temperature and token limit, cutting token use without retraining the model.
evidence.title: DiffAdapt: Difficulty-Adaptive Reasoning for Token-Efficient LLM Inference

evidence.note: vStream trains a lightweight linear estimator to predict counterfactual ablation effects of image regions from cached attention features, so a multimodal reasoning model's visual grounding can be displayed while it reasons rather than recomputed afterwards, at 0.024 s per 10 tokens against 1.9-2.8 s for causal baselines.
evidence.title: Real-Time Visual Attribution Streaming in Thinking Model

evidence.note: Diagnoses why adding a length penalty to GRPO degrades accuracy — the group-relative advantage can turn correct-but-long rollouts negative — and fixes it by normalising the reward of correct rollouts only against other correct rollouts.
evidence.title: DRPO: Efficient Reasoning via Decoupled Reward Policy Optimization

evidence.note: A*-Thought treats a long reasoning trace as a search tree over reasoning spans and uses A* search with a bidirectional importance score to select a short, high-information subset of it as supervised fine-tuning data for compressed reasoning.
evidence.title: A*-Thought: Efficient Reasoning via Bidirectional Compression for Low-Resource Settings

evidence.note: ReBalance is a training-free inference-time steering method that reads a reasoning model's token confidence to detect overthinking or underthinking and applies a hidden-state steering vector to shorten or extend the chain of thought accordingly.
evidence.title: Efficient Reasoning with Balanced Thinking

evidence.note: Ada-R1 merges a long-CoT and a short-CoT model into one hybrid, then applies two levels of preference training so the model first picks a reasoning style per problem and then prefers the shorter correct trace within that style, cutting average reasoning length by about 51% on five maths datasets.
evidence.title: Ada-R1: Hybrid-CoT via Bi-Level Adaptive Reasoning Optimization

evidence.note: Trains Qwen3-8B to split its chain of thought into concurrently decoded threads that spawn and join, so the critical path is shorter than a sequential trace of the same total length, using a trie-based rollout that runs on stock autoregressive inference engines.
evidence.title: ThreadWeaver: Adaptive Threading for Efficient Parallel Reasoning in Language Models

evidence.note: DEER is a training-free decoding method that watches for the points where a reasoning model switches thought chains, prompts it for a trial answer there, and terminates the chain of thought when the trial answer's token confidence exceeds a threshold.
evidence.title: Dynamic Early Exit in Reasoning Models

name: OlympiadBench
